ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, points X, Y, Z form a right triangle, and XY and YZ have a right-angle mark at Y; points X, W, Z also form a right triangle, and XW and WZ have a right-angle mark at W. Segment XZ is the hypotenuse common to the two triangles. The figure marks XW = 7. At point Z, the angle between ZX and ZY is labeled 41°, and the angle between ZX and ZW is also labeled 41°. Reasoning: Triangle XYZ and triangle XWZ are both right triangles, share hypotenuse XZ, and have equal acute angles 41° at Z. Therefore the two right triangles are congruent by “hypotenuse and one acute angle.” Among corresponding sides, the side opposite the 41° angle in triangle XYZ is XY, and the side opposite the 41° angle in triangle XWZ is XW, so XY = XW = 7.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: points X, Y, Z form a right triangle with a right angle at Y, and points X, W, Z form another right triangle with a right angle at W. Segment XW is labeled 7. The diagonal XZ is shared by both triangles. At Z, the angle between ZY and ZX is marked 41°, and the angle between ZX and ZW is also marked 41°. From the text, the required length is XY. Since triangles XYZ and XWZ are right triangles sharing hypotenuse XZ and having the same acute angle at Z, they are congruent by right-triangle hypotenuse-angle congruence. Therefore the side opposite the 41° angle in triangle XYZ, namely XY, equals the corresponding side opposite the 41° angle in triangle XWZ, namely XW. Thus XY = XW = 7.
